## TL;DR

Remote browser shot captures logged completion and wrote `result.json` but often left the runner container alive at ~0% CPU, so Mac-side handoffs blocked on container exit, timed out, and retried into duplicate capture queues. This task adds an explicit bounded runner exit, Mac-side force-collection when `result.json` is stable, periodic and startup reapers for completed shot containers, handoff-time cancellation of stale captures, and observable debug events. Review pass 12 required one more fix: the `validate.sh` startup reaper must not abort a new validation run when transient `docker ps` / `docker logs` inspection fails under `set -euo pipefail`.

## Work and rationale

The failure mode was consistent on Tailscale runners (thinkpad, bee, mini): logs showed `[browser-capture] runner browser capture completed`, yet `docker ps` still listed the container for fifteen minutes or more until someone ran `docker rm -f`. The Mac control plane waited for the container process to exit; handoff verification hit “timed out waiting for the task's browser capture” and retried, leaving another idle container behind each time.

The runner entry in `capture-browser.ts` now performs best-effort preview cleanup inside a short timeout, writes `result.json` atomically, logs completion, and calls `process.exit` so an open Playwright handle or timer cannot keep Bun alive. On the Mac, `remote-validation.ts` polls for a stable `result.json` (and matching completion log semantics), collects artifacts, force-removes the container, and records a remote-validation event. A shared reaper path extends #1049’s hang watchdog to shot captures that logged completion and have been idle past a grace period. Failed handoffs cancel that task’s queued and in-flight browser captures so retries do not queue behind duplicates.

Startup reaping in `validate.sh` mirrors the periodic reaper: before a new run, still-running capture containers that already finished and have been quiet with low CPU are removed, with `[reaper]` log lines parsed back into task events. Earlier review passes hardened `docker rm -f` failure reporting and periodic reaper observability; pass 12 noted that the inspection commands at the top of that loop were still strict under `set -e`.

## Approaches tried

We first relied on setting `process.exitCode` and natural process exit; subprocess tests with a live timer proved that insufficient. Mac-side collection initially waited on container exit only; force-collection on stable `result.json` was added as belt-and-braces. Reaper logic was centralized in TypeScript for the periodic tick while keeping a bash startup sweep on runners that do not run the Mac daemon.

For the startup reaper, review pass 9 asked to contain `docker rm -f` failures; we assigned `rm_code` in one assignment and only emit success markers after verifying removal. Pass 12 asked for the same containment on inspection: wrapping the loop in `set +e` / `set -e` and guarding `docker logs --since` with `|| continue`, plus a script-text regression test so the pattern cannot regress silently.

## Challenges and blockers

Merge churn with `main` and repeated handoff gate races (HEAD moving during check, format failures) consumed several turns without changing the core design. Engineering report section requirements and stale report bindings blocked review until drafts matched the checked tree. Scoped `repoos check` also surfaced an accidental `PipelineCard.vue` regression (`color: var(--muted)` on text roles); that was reverted to `var(--txt-dim)` so the hardcoded-color gate passes without widening #1060’s server scope.

Live verification on physical runners was not performed in this session; behavior is covered by unit tests and script-contract tests. A human with SSH to thinkpad/bee/mini should confirm containers exit promptly after the next deploy.

## Key learnings

Completed work and a exited process are different signals: for remote captures, `result.json` plus a completion log line is the authoritative done signal; container lifetime is best-effort. Any bash maintenance that runs before the main `validate.sh` gate must treat Docker inspection as fallible—`set -euo pipefail` and unguarded command substitutions will skip validation entirely on a blip. When fixing hang reapers, grep sibling paths for the same pattern (startup vs periodic vs force-collect) and test the class, not one line. Finally, surface-token CSS variables (`--muted`) must not be used for text color; text tokens like `--txt-dim` or `--muted-foreground` belong at call sites.
